document_name: GBV News AI Storage and Supabase Implementation Context
purpose: Machine-readable implementation context for Codex/AI agents implementing persistence, GCS storage, Supabase PostgreSQL tracking, collection runs, and migration away from local collected-data storage.

title: Use Google Cloud Storage for all collected and generated pipeline files
decision: Collected research data must not use local filesystem persistence as the durable storage layer. Raw source responses, normalized JSON, collection-run artifacts, reports, logs, and reusable CDX/index cache artifacts should be written to Google Cloud Storage.
supersedes: Current repository behavior that writes collected data beneath data/trials/ on the local filesystem.
rationale: Application is intended for GCP deployment.
App Engine local filesystem is not suitable as durable application storage.
Research artifacts require durable object storage and reproducible lineage.
Keeping object payloads outside PostgreSQL avoids turning the relational database into a file store.

title: Use Supabase PostgreSQL as the structured tracking and query layer
decision: Supabase PostgreSQL stores structured article metadata, collection-run state, object URIs, processing lineage, and later research entities. It does not store raw HTML or the complete processed JSON artifact.

title: Use SQLAlchemy and psycopg for backend database access
decision: Python collection code and the future Flask application should access Supabase PostgreSQL using SQLAlchemy and psycopg rather than using the Supabase Python Data API as the primary persistence layer.

title: Raw object persistence precedes parsing
invariant: A successfully fetched source response must be durably written to GCS before its parsed/normalized representation is treated as persisted.

overwrite_policy: Parser and content-addressed paths preserve changed extraction versions without overwriting older research output.

note: The user has chosen no durable local collected-data storage. Run checkpoint/report/cache artifacts therefore also need a GCS-backed implementation.

developer caches that are not research records
implementation_requirement: Production and real trial/monthly collection code must not rely on local files for resume, deduplication, raw persistence, processed persistence, or run history.

decision: Trial runs use the same durable architecture as monthly runs.
requirements: Every trial run must have a collection_runs row.
Trial raw HTML goes directly to the raw GCS bucket.
Trial normalized JSON goes directly to the processed GCS bucket.
Each successfully indexed trial article gets an articles row or resolves an existing one.
Each distinct persisted extraction gets an article_versions row linked to the trial collection_run_id.
Trial data is not treated as disposable merely because it is a trial; it remains traceable and can later be promoted/reviewed according to research rules.

decision: Retrospective monthly runs use GCS for all durable files and Supabase for indexed run/article state.
requirements: Resolve or create collection_runs before processing articles.
Store exact non-secret run configuration in collection_runs.configuration.
Keep publication_month based on source publication metadata, not scrape/archive time.
Connect each article_versions row to collection_run_id.
Resume logic must be redesigned to read durable checkpoint state from GCS and/or Supabase instead of local run directories.

statuses.raw_stored: Raw source object is durably present in GCS. Parsing/processed persistence may not yet be complete.
statuses.processed: Raw object exists and processed normalized JSON is durably present in GCS.
statuses.indexed: Required GCS artifacts exist and structured Supabase article/version persistence has completed.
statuses.failed: A processing/indexing step failed; retain already-written raw evidence and capture a non-secret processing_error.

rules: article_versions has UNIQUE(article_id UUID, content_hash, parser_version).
GCS raw writes should use create-if-absent/generation preconditions where feasible.
A retry must resolve existing logical article rows rather than create duplicates.
A retry of the same content with the same parser should resolve the existing version rather than create another version.
A new parser version or changed normalized content may create a new article_versions row while keeping the same logical article.
Use timezone-aware Python datetimes for TIMESTAMPTZ columns.
Do not silently assume UTC for source dates explicitly known to have unknown timezone.
Preserve original source date string in published_at_raw.
Set publication_timezone='unknown' and publication_date_needs_review=true when absolute publication time cannot be safely established.
Represent month-only database fields using the first day of the month.

repository_pattern: Database persistence should be isolated behind repository/service functions rather than embedded in publisher parser modules.
transaction_rule: Article upsert/resolution and ArticleVersion insertion should be transactionally coordinated after GCS object persistence.

explicit_omission: No production LocalStorage backend is required for collected research data under the current decision. Unit tests may use in-memory/fake/temporary test storage.

credential_policy: Use Application Default Credentials/service identity on GCP. Do not commit service-account JSON keys or Supabase credentials.
local_dev_policy: Local development may use ADC and an ignored .env for configuration, but real collected objects still go to GCS.

rules: Collected GBV research artifacts must not be made public by default.
Supabase RLS is enabled on the initial tables and no public policies are intentionally created.
Automatically exposing newly created research tables through the Data API should remain disabled.
Secrets must not be written into collection_runs.configuration, GCS metadata, logs, JSON artifacts, Git, AGENTS.md, README.md, or AI context documents.

title: How later research entities should attach to the ingestion core
relationships: annotations -> articles and/or article_versions depending on whether the annotation targets logical article content or a specific processed version
predictions -> article_versions + model_versions so predictions remain reproducible against exact processed input and model version
locations/geocodes -> article_versions or prediction/review entities with provenance and privacy controls
reviews -> preserve human correction separately from machine predictions
dataset_versions -> exact sets of article_version IDs rather than mutable latest article state
principle: Never overwrite historical model predictions with human corrections; preserve original predictions and review/annotation separately.

criteria: Running a bounded trial creates/uses one collection_runs row.
No real trial article HTML is durably written beneath data/trials/raw.
Every successful fetch that proceeds to parsing has a raw GCS object URI.
Every successfully normalized article has a processed GCS JSON object URI.
Supabase articles contains one logical row per source/canonical article.
Supabase article_versions links the logical article, producing run, raw object, processed object, content hash and parser version.
Rerunning the same trial does not duplicate articles or identical article_versions.
Monthly progress/resume works without relying on durable local run files.
Existing offline parser tests continue to pass.
New storage/database tests verify GCS failure, DB failure, retry and idempotency behavior.

expected_behavior: Do not parse/index the article as successfully persisted. Record/log failure at run level and retry according to collector policy.
Keep raw object in GCS. No processed URI is required. Preserve enough run/error information for later reprocessing.
Keep both GCS artifacts. Retry database indexing idempotently; do not re-fetch merely because the DB transaction failed.
Resolve existing articles.id UUID using deterministic identity/unique keys, then insert or resolve article_versions.

current_behavior: Repository currently persists raw HTML, processed JSON, progress.json, monthly_counts.csv, logs and CDX caches to local data/trials paths.
target_behavior: All durable collection artifacts move to GCS, while Supabase PostgreSQL becomes the queryable index and run/lineage tracker.
